subject: Business Models
title: Instagram's Pre-Launch Pivot
description: A quick win: understand Instagram's Pre-Launch Pivot.

hook.text: Instagram was originally called Burbn—a check-in app like Foursquare. Nobody used the check-in feature.

buildup.text: Kevin Systrom noticed one feature got all the engagement: photo sharing with filters.

discovery.text: They stripped everything else out. Burbn became Instagram: photos, filters, sharing. Nothing else.

twist.text: Instagram hit 1 million users in 2 months. Facebook bought it for $1 billion 18 months after launch.

climax.text: The pivot wasn't grand strategy—it was listening to user behavior and removing everything they didn't use.

punchline.text: Check-in app nobody used. Stripped it to photos only. $1 billion in 18 months.

quiz.question: What was Instagram's original product called?

details.summary: Instagram started as Burbn, a complex location-based social app. Before launching publicly, founders Systrom and Krieger noticed users loved the photo-sharing feature most and stripped the product down to just photos and filters, creating a focused app that reached one million users in two months.
details.whyItMatters: Instagram's pivot shows that successful products often emerge from ruthlessly cutting features, not adding them. The willingness to abandon months of work on Burbn to focus on one beloved feature led to a billion-dollar acquisition by Facebook in.
takeaways: Burbn was stripped down to just photo sharing based on user behavior data
Simplicity and focus drove one million users within two months of launch
Facebook acquired Instagram for one billion dollars just two years later

faq.question: What made Instagram's founders decide to pivot from Burbn?
faq.answer: They analyzed user behavior and discovered that photo sharing was by far the most used feature of the complex Burbn app. Instead of improving underused features, they made the bold decision to strip everything else away and build the entire product around photography.

faq.question: What lesson does the Instagram pivot teach about product strategy?
faq.answer: Find the one feature users love most and make it the entire product. Simplicity beats feature richness. User behavior data matters more than founder vision. The willingness to abandon sunk costs in favor of what actually works separates successful pivots from failures.
